chapter: Flip Benson, Grand Rapids and the Army
title: Marriage, Grand Rapids and a WPA band
summary: Ware marries, stays in Grand Rapids, and plays in a WPA band at Fort Custer until the draft breaks it up.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: You got married and stayed in Grand Rapids.
And worked in a WPA band there. What kinds of things were you doing?

Well, we were playing -- this is 1941 -- the war had broken out, and so I got married, and Flip was going out to the west coast, and I didn't want to leave my wife, so some musicians around Grand Rapids said, "Well, maybe we can get you in one of the WPA bands here" -- so I put in for it, and they got me on.

What it was -- you go and play, you play at community centers, and I think Fort Custer had opened up, and we played there on Tuesdays and Fridays for the soldiers, you know, at the USO hall. Until our band just started -- the draft was grabbing them all; we had a big band, and they were grabbing the cats right and left. And I think it was in 1942, they dissolved it. Too many of them had to get in defense work.
